findings.issue: The code accesses `process.env` in a client‑side React component. In the browser `process` is undefined, causing a `ReferenceError` and preventing the app from rendering.

API route definitions are missing a leading slash (e.g., `route("api/v1/chat/completions", ...)`). This makes the routes resolve relative to the current path, so the intended endpoints (`/api/v1/...`) will not match and return 404.
findings.fix:
Add a leading slash to each API route path:
```ts
export default [
  index("routes/landing.tsx"),
  route("/auth", "routes/auth.tsx"),
  route("/logout", "routes/logout.tsx"),
  route("/api/v1/chat/completions", "routes/api.v1.chat.completions.ts"),
  route("/api/v1/models", "routes/api.v1.models.ts"),
  route("/dashboard", "routes/dashboard/layout.tsx", [
    index("routes/dashboard/home.tsx"),
    route("chat", "routes/dashboard/chat.tsx"),
    // ... other dashboard routes
  ]),
] satisfies RouteConfig;
```
